title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Palau: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Palau: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Palau: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in the Republic of Palau, medical reporting flows through Belau National Hospital while civil vital records, estate filings, and Apostille authentication operate primarily through the Clerk of Courts and national agencies in Koror and Ngerulmud [2][6][9]. Because Palau is a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention and is transitioning toward dedicated formal Probate Rules, families should follow current statutory court and Social Security procedures closely [1][2][7].

steps.title: Immediate medical certification, hospital liaison, and emergency services
steps.html:
• Call 911 for all emergencies (488-1411 for Fire and Ambulance; 488-1622 for Police) if death occurs outside a healthcare facility [11].
  • Coordinate the medical certificate of cause of death through Ministry of Health and Human Services (MHHS) / Belau National Hospital in Koror (+680 488-2552 / 2553 Administration; +680 488-2558 Emergency Room) [10][11].
  • Confirm hospital release requirements, public-health clearances, and burial or international remains transport arrangements early with the treating facility and relevant diplomatic missions if non-resident transport applies [10][11].

steps.title: Death registration and certified certificates via the Clerk of Courts
steps.html:
• Register and request official Death Certificates through Office of the Clerk of Courts (Palau Supreme Court), whose Vital Statistics division in Koror (+680 488-2607 / 3331 / 4979; Ngerulmud +680 767-2607; Monday to Friday 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM) coordinates vital record updates alongside hospital death notifications [2][3][5].
  • Under published Palau Judiciary fee schedules and FAQs, certified Death Certificate copies cost US$ 2.00 in person or US$ 15.00 for off-island requests [2][4].
  • Obtain multiple certified copies immediately, because Social Security survivor filings, court estate petitions, bank closures, and Apostille requests each require official certified extracts [1][2][8].

steps.title: Republic of Palau Social Security Administration (ROPSSA) survivor benefits
steps.html:
• Notify Republic of Palau Social Security Administration (ROPSSA) (P.O. Box 679, Koror, Palau 96940; Tel +680 488-2457) and verify Healthcare Fund (HCF) records (+680 488-1904) [8][9].
  • Check survivor benefit eligibility against ROPSSA insured-status thresholds: a deceased contributor is 'fully insured' with at least one quarter of coverage per year between age 21 and death (or 38 quarters under standard retirement tables), 'currently insured' with at least 8 quarters in the preceding 13 quarters, or 'permanently insured' with 120 quarters (30 years) [8].
  • File the official survivor application together with a certified Death Certificate, marriage certificate, children's birth certificates, and guardianship or claimant ID documents [2][8].

steps.title: Estate petitions, court divisions, and tax clearances
steps.html:
• Open an estate using downloadable forms filed with Office of the Clerk of Courts, noting from the Palau Judiciary's 2026 consultation announcement (# 26-172) that Palau currently lacks dedicated standalone Probate Rules (with draft rules under public comment through January 2027), so petitions follow existing civil, Supreme Court Trial Division, Court of Common Pleas (for civil claims up to US$ 10,000 excluding land disputes), and Land Court procedures [2][6][7].
  • For low-income residents requiring legal assistance with estate filings or guardianship, contact Micronesian Legal Services Corporation (MLSC) in Palau (+680 488-2473 / 2474) [2].
  • Verify final wage, business gross revenue, or Palau Goods and Services Tax (PGST) obligations through national tax authorities and the employer's payroll office; Palau taxes wages and business gross revenues rather than imposing an inheritance or estate duty [9].

steps.title: Hague Apostille authentication and notifying institutions
steps.html:
• Because the Republic of Palau is a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (in force since 23 June 2020), certified Palau Death Certificates and court grants destined for other Convention countries can be authenticated by Apostille through Palau's designated Competent Authorities: the Minister of State (P.O. Box 6051, Koror; +680 767-2408 / 2490) or the Clerk of Courts, Palau Supreme Court [1].
  • Verify foreign destination language or translation rules with the receiving bank, pension fund, or registry before dispatching Apostilled originals overseas [1].
  • Notify Palau banks, insurers, utilities, employers, and state land offices in writing using certified Death Certificates and court letters [2][6][7].

contacts.name: Office of the Clerk of Courts (Palau Supreme Court)
contacts.note: Issues certified Death Certificates ($2.00 local / $15.00 off-island), accepts estate petitions, and serves as a Competent Authority for 1961 Hague Apostilles. Ngerulmud: +680 767-2607.

contacts.name: Republic of Palau Social Security Administration (ROPSSA)
contacts.note: Administers surviving spouse and dependent child benefits; Healthcare Fund (HCF) Office: +680 488-1904.

contacts.name: Ministry of Health and Human Services (MHHS)
contacts.note: Operates Belau National Hospital in Koror (+680 488-2552/2553 Admin; +680 488-2558 Emergency Room; 911 emergency dispatch).

contacts.name: Micronesian Legal Services Corporation (MLSC)
contacts.note: Provides legal aid for eligible indigent residents in civil and estate matters (+680 488-2473 / 488-2474).
